resources.string: This app opens the Ruzzco system that runs on the shop PC. Keep this phone on the shop Wi-Fi.
Sales that haven\'t synced yet stay with the old address. Before you switch, check that the POS shows everything synced. That includes moving from :3000 to the secure address (https, :3443).
Looking for the shop PC on %1$s…
No Ruzzco server answered on this Wi-Fi. Check that the shop PC is on and running Ruzzco, or type its address below.
This phone isn\'t on a Wi-Fi network. Connect it to the shop Wi-Fi, then tap Find again.

plurals.name: find_found
plurals.item: Found the shop PC. Tap it to connect.
Found %d Ruzzco servers. Tap the one to use.

resources.string: The address is the shop PC\'s Wi-Fi address and :3000. On the PC, run ipconfig and look under Wi-Fi for the IPv4 Address.
That doesn\'t look like an address. Type it like 192.168.1.19:3000.
No answer from %1$s. Check that the shop PC is on and running Ruzzco, and that this phone is on the shop Wi-Fi.
Something answered at %1$s, but it isn\'t the Ruzzco system. Check the number after the colon (usually 3000).
Connected. The shop PC\'s database isn\'t running, so some pages may show errors.

%1$s didn\'t answer. Check that the shop PC is on and running Ruzzco, and that this phone is on the shop Wi-Fi. Sales already saved on this phone are kept there only: they\'re recorded once it reaches the shop PC again, with the POS open.
This phone doesn\'t trust the shop certificate for %1$s. Rebuild the app on the shop PC after running npm run https there, or install the certificate on this phone from the PC\'s address with :3080.
No app on this phone can open that link.
No app on this phone can pick a file.
